data.name: The Quiet Index
data.subtitle: An archive mystery
data.hint: The chart opens the cabinet. Compare the restored register with an independent boundary record, then ask the residents how they want their names handled.
data.intro: Tomorrow the city will demolish the river quarter. Tonight its archive claims nobody ever lived there. Archivist Iva asks you to find the missing register before the hearing.

rooms.name: Reading Room
rooms.description: The public catalogue ends abruptly at the letter R. Iva waits beside an empty display case.

rooms.name: Closed Stacks
rooms.description: Dusty boxes lean against a locked cabinet. A handwritten filing chart hangs by the door.

rooms.name: Bindery
rooms.description: A press, a shallow water tray and a roll of archival tissue occupy the old worktable.

rooms.name: Hearing Chamber
rooms.description: A microphone faces the council's sealed demolition order. Residents gather outside.

actions.label: Iva: ask for help
actions.text: Iva admits she hid the register from a former director. She gives you her stacks pass and says the cabinet code is impressed on the old chart.
actions.journal: The filing chart bears a cabinet impression.

actions.label: Iva: challenge the silence
actions.text: Iva says the director ordered the register concealed. She gives you her stacks pass, ashamed she obeyed. Look for an impression on the filing chart, she says.
actions.journal: The filing chart bears a cabinet impression.

actions.label: Enter the closed stacks
actions.text: The pass opens the gate.

actions.label: Return to the reading room
actions.text: You return to the catalogue.

actions.label: Examine the filing chart
actions.text: The chart says the river plants are filed by their four-letter name. Pressure marks spell REED; make a rubbing to read the setting at the cabinet.

actions.label: Make a rubbing of the chart
actions.text: Using a scrap from the chart's edge, you copy the marks.

actions.label: Set the cabinet to REED
actions.text: The cabinet clicks open. Inside is a water-damaged fragment listing the river quarter's families.
actions.journal: The fragment needs careful repair before it can be submitted.

actions.label: Inspect the survey index
actions.text: A note cross-references the river trust to survey 14, filed in the bindery under maps. A name alone will not prove the boundary.
actions.journal: Survey 14 in the bindery connects the trust to the river boundary.

actions.label: Go to the bindery
actions.text: You carry the evidence to the worktable.

actions.label: Return to the stacks
actions.text: You return between the shelves.

actions.label: Find survey 14 among the maps
actions.text: Survey 14 bears the trust seal and outlines the quarter in the demolition order. You copy it for the hearing.
actions.journal: Survey 14 independently identifies the threatened land as trust property.

actions.label: Take archival tissue
actions.text: The thin tissue can support fragile paper without obscuring the ink.

actions.label: Repair the fragment with tissue
actions.text: You support the fragile sheet with tissue. It names the river community land trust, but a separate boundary survey would connect that trust to the threatened land.
actions.journal: The register proves the land belongs to a community trust.

actions.label: Enter the hearing chamber
actions.text: The hearing is about to begin.

actions.label: Return to the reading room
actions.text: There is still time to search.

actions.label: Ask residents about the names
actions.text: The residents disagree about publicity. Their advocate explains that a redacted public claim can expose the land record while withholding family names; the full register must still be filed under seal.
actions.journal: A redacted claim and a sealed register are a third option; residents disagree on publicity.

actions.label: Compare the register with survey 14
actions.text: The seal and boundary match. The advocate can now distinguish the trust claim from an unsupported list of names.
actions.journal: The restored register and survey 14 corroborate the trust claim.

actions.label: Submit the register publicly
actions.text: Despite some residents’ reservations, you read the names aloud. The council suspends demolition pending a hearing; the exposed families cannot take their names back. Iva adds her account to the public record.
actions.journal: The names are public, despite disagreement; the community has time to defend its land.

actions.label: Publish the boundary, seal the names
actions.text: The advocate files the full register under seal and publishes the survey and a redacted claim. The council suspends demolition pending a hearing. The public sees the boundary, but must trust the sealed evidence.
actions.journal: The boundary is public; the names remain sealed, and the claim still awaits a hearing.

actions.label: Give the register to the residents' advocate
actions.text: The advocate files the deed under seal at the residents' request. The council suspends demolition; the families will choose when to tell their story.
actions.journal: The claim is protected and the residents retain control of their names.

victory.title: The record survives
victory.epilogue: The demolition is suspended pending a hearing. The record of your decision remains below and in the journal.
